'''''Lotus hirsutus''''', also known by the [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] ''Dorycnium hirsutum'',<ref name=POWO_503681-1/> common name: '''canary clover'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''hairy canary-clover''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=DOHI2|taxon=Dorycnium hirsutum|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the legume [[family (botany)|family]] Fabaceae.<ref name=POWO_503681-1/>

==Description==
It is a low-growing, domed semi-[[evergreen]] [[subshrub]], reaching on average {{convert|20|-|50|cm}} in height. Its habit is erect, green, hairy and branched. The silver leaves are [[sessility (botany)|sessile]], alternate and quite fuzzy. The flowers are white veined pinkish-red, in terminal umbels composed of four to ten flowers. The flowering period extends from May through July. The fruits are cylindrical reddish brown seed pods.<ref name = RHSPF/>

==Distribution and habitat==
This plant is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]], from [[Portugal]] to [[Turkey]] and south to northern Africa.<ref name=POWO_503681-1/>

The typical habitat of this sub-shrub is grassland, in well-drained soil. Plants can be found at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1500|m}}.

==Cultivation==
This plant is found in cultivation. Though hardy down to {{convert|-10 |C|F|abbr=on}}, it requires a sheltered spot in full sun. In the [[United Kingdom]] it has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/80172/i-Lotus-hirsutus-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Lotus hirsutus'' | accessdate= 29 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 
| page = 62 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 25 March 2018}}</ref>
